chunks: Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man performs tayammum, then enters into the salat, and he had sought water but was unable to obtain it; then water is brought when he enters into the salat. He said: “He continues in the salat, and know that it is not appropriate for anyone to perform tayammum except at the end of the time.”

As for what has been narrated in the reports that he should break off from it so long as he has not bowed, its meaning is that if the time is extended enough for him to break off and perform wudu with water, then in such a case breaking off becomes obligatory for him, because he entered the salat before its proper time, since its time is at the end of the time and when the period has become constrained, such that if he does not perform it then it will pass him by. But when the time is extended, it is obligatory for him to break off and perform wudu, according to what the reports have conveyed. This is indicated by the narration of al-Bazanṭī and his statement that tayammum should only be done at the end of the time. We have also clarified this previously in what Muḥammad ibn Muslim and Zurārah narrated, and that tayammum is not permissible except at the end of the time, and among what has been narrated concerning that.

key_terms.آخِرِ الْوَقْتِ: the end of the prayer time, when tayammum becomes proper in this context
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat being performed after purification
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports used in deriving the ruling
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water required for wudu (ablution) when available
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum as a substitute purification when water was unavailable
key_terms.يَمْضِي: he continues and proceeds without breaking the prayer
key_terms.يَنْصَرِفُ: he breaks off or turns away from the prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone performs tayammum and then finds water after starting salat, should he continue or break the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who performs tayammum, begins salat, and then finds water. The Imam عليه السلام states that he continues the prayer, while the accompanying juristic explanation reconciles this with other reports by distinguishing between a constrained prayer time and an extended one. The passage emphasizes that tayammum is only proper at the end of the prayer time when access to water remains unavailable.
